name: Store Blåmann
access: Kvaløya, ~35 min from Tromsø, road to sea level
note: Sea-to-summit on Kvaløya. The classic is the NE side; the N face is a serious step up. Steep upper headwall holds wind slab — check the Tromsø bulletin for persistent weak layers before committing.

name: Tromsdalstinden
note: The town mountain and the best-value big vertical in the region. Broad W flank skis well in spring corn; the upper bowl is a wind-loading collector.

name: Hamperokken
note: One of northern Norway's great lines. The NE couloir/face is sustained 40°+ with real consequence. Wants a locked-up snowpack and a stable forecast, not a maybe.

name: Rørnestinden
access: Roadside on the Lyngen west shore
note: Fjord-to-summit in a single clean pitch — the tour people fly in for. Skis best mid-spring when the lower slopes corn up in the afternoon.

name: Goalsevárri (Goalsevarri)
note: Big rolling west face, forgiving angle, huge sightlines. A strong 'danger 3' fallback when the steeper Lyngen lines are off.

name: Store Jægervasstind
note: Glaciated, committing, the full alpine feel of the Lyngen Alps. Rope and crevasse kit; don't treat it as a ski tour with a summit attached.

name: Fastdalstinden
note: Long sustained fall-line skiing from near the summit to the fjord. Upper section steepens — good barometer of how the wind has worked the slabs.

name: Storgalten
note: Sun-facing and skis into corn early. Good pick when the north-facing snowpack is still holding a persistent problem.

name: Segla
note: Small numbers, big exposure. The east flank is skiable; everything near the ridge is cliff. Short enough to combine with a second Senja objective.

name: Breidtinden
note: Senja's highest, and a genuine alpine feel for a coastal peak. Holds cold snow late into spring.

name: Keipen
note: Steep-sided classic with several aspects to choose from once you're up — useful flexibility on a marginal day.

name: Higravstinden
note: The Lofoten prize: sea to 1146 m through steep, complex terrain. Serious avalanche terrain with no easy bail once committed.

name: Geitgaljen
note: Often the best-skiing big line in Lofoten. Sun-affected: time it so the south face has softened but not gone punchy.

name: Stornappstind
note: Short, steep, straight to the sea. Holds dry snow thanks to the north aspect — a good storm-cycle option when cloud is down.

name: Rombakstøtta
note: Big fjord-side vertical with a defined upper face. Narvik's everyday objective when the resort is wind-hold.

name: Storsteinsfjellet
note: Glaciated high-alpine day near the Swedish border. Long approach, big reward, rope required.

name: Sulitjelma area
note: Glacier-backed border peaks with a long spring season and very few people. Strong option when the coast is getting rained on.

name: Kirketaket
note: Romsdal's signature tour — long, consistent, and it keeps its quality late. The upper bowl loads hard in NW wind.

name: Store Venjetinden
note: Ski-mountaineering, not a tour. Steep, exposed, rappel likely. Only with a locked snowpack and the right partners.

name: Slogen
note: The Sunnmøre icon: fjord to summit, sustained and exposed near the top. Wants a settled spring pack and an early start.

name: Skårasalen
note: Perhaps the best pure descent in Sunnmøre — 1500 m of fall-line to the fjord. Cornices along the top ridge.

name: Kolåstinden
note: Steep, aesthetic, and a real summit. Bootpack near the top most seasons.

name: Snota
note: Trollheimen's best-known line and often overlooked while everyone drives to Romsdal. Big north-facing bowls.

name: Trollhetta
note: Three-summit massif with several independent descents — easy to adapt the plan to the day's danger rating.

name: Fannaråken
note: High, long season, and the summit hut view. Glacier terrain on parts of the route — carry the kit.

name: Galdhøpiggen
note: Norway's roof. More a glacier ski-mountaineering day than a steep descent, but the spring corn off the top is worth it.

name: Store Ringstind
note: Steep north-side ski-mountaineering in Hurrungane. Glacier, no-fall terrain, rope and a genuinely stable pack.

name: Skogshorn
note: Southern Norway's most-skied steep-ish objective. North face holds cold snow; the standard route is far more forgiving than the face.

links.title: Tips for ski touring in Hemsedal

name: Gaustatoppen
access: Stavsro parking on Fv651 between Rjukan and Tuddal (about 1175 m)
note: Telemark's highest summit and the southern anchor of the list: reliable snow, big views and broad, open flanks on the normal route from Stavsro (about 4.5 km). Position and height checked against Kartverket's terrain model (1882 m).

name: Njulla (Nuolja)
note: The Abisko warm-up: short approach, several aspects, and it's where you read the snowpack before heading into Kårsavagge.

name: Låktatjåkko
note: Hut-based base for the whole Riksgränsen zone. Rolling terrain plus steeper north-facing options off the shoulders.

name: Kårsavagge / Kårsatjåkka
access: Ski in from Abisko, hut at Kårsavagge
note: The best multi-day pocket in the Swedish north — a valley ringed with north-facing couloirs and faces. Commit a couple of nights.

name: Kebnekaise Sydtoppen
note: Sweden's highest. Västra leden as the ski line; big, exposed, and weather is the main hazard as much as the snow.

name: Duolbagorni (Tolpagorni)
note: The crater peak — steep, dramatic, and the photograph everyone knows. Serious slab terrain in the bowl.

name: Kaskasatjåkka
note: Big north-side lines and glacier terrain above Tarfala. Among the most alpine skiing in Sweden.

name: Nallo & Sälka couloirs
note: A dense cluster of couloirs off the Kungsleden huts. Classic Swedish ski-mountaineering week; nothing is a quick bail.

name: Norra Sytertoppen
note: Norra Storfjället's high point and the anchor of the Hemavan touring zone. Long approach, big open faces up top.

name: Hemavan–Tärnaby roadside fjäll
note: The most convenient touring in Sweden: lap after lap straight from the car, with a real bulletin covering it. Ideal storm-day terrain at modest angles.

name: Marsfjället
note: Remote, quiet, and rarely tracked. Self-sufficiency matters more here than technical difficulty.

name: Kittelfjäll backcountry
note: Small village, disproportionate snow. Short, repeatable north-facing runs — the Swedish powder cliché for a reason.

name: Storsnasen (Snasahögarna)
note: The Jämtland benchmark: north-facing bowls and gullies that hold cold snow, with genuine slab terrain. Read the Södra Jämtlandsfjällen bulletin carefully.

name: Getryggen
note: Short lines, quick laps, and the classic 'let's see what the snowpack is doing' objective from Storulvån.

name: Tväråklumpen
note: Couloir country — the steepest easily-reached skiing in Jämtland. Small terrain that behaves like big terrain.

name: Storsylen
note: The most alpine skyline in southern Sweden. Hut-based, weather-exposed, and worth the ski-in.

name: Åreskutan off-piste laps
note: Lift access to touring terrain on the back side. Convenient, tracked fast, and the resort's own assessment is not the bulletin — the two cover different ground.

name: Helags
note: Sweden's southernmost glacier and the best big-mountain feel south of Lappland. North side holds quality snow into May.

name: Lill-Helags couloirs
note: Tight, steep and the reason people stay at Helags for a week rather than a night.

name: Ramundberget–Bruksvallarna fjäll
note: Low-angle, high-frequency terrain. Where the southern season starts and where you go when the danger rating is ugly.

name: Lillsylen
access: Sylarnas fjällstation (ski in from Storulvån, about 16 km)
note: The second summit of the Sylarna massif, just north of Storsylen. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Storsola (Templet)
access: Sylarnas fjällstation (ski in from Storulvån, about 16 km)
note: The big southern summit of Sylarna, also called Templet, with a small glacier. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Sylskalsstöten
access: Sylarnas fjällstation (ski in from Storulvån, about 16 km)
note: East of Storsola; a less crowded summit on the Swedish side of Sylarna. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Vaktklumpen
access: Sylarnas fjällstation (ski in from Storulvån, about 16 km)
note: Northern outlier of Sylarna, close to the fjällstation; a shorter day. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Herrklumpen
access: Sylarnas fjällstation (ski in from Storulvån, about 16 km)
note: Low summit about 1 km from Sylarnas fjällstation; a short lap or a bad-weather option. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Bandaklumpen
access: Sylarnas fjällstation (ski in from Storulvån, about 16 km); the summit is on the Norwegian side
note: West of Storsylen, just across the border in Norway. Uses the Swedish Södra Jämtlandsfjällen bulletin, the nearest one. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Lillsnasen
note: Western neighbour of Storsnasen in the Snasahögarna, 1.5 km from it. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Miektjieburrientjahke
note: Rounded summit south-east of Storulvån, in the Vålådalen nature reserve. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Laptentjahke
note: South of Storulvån, in the Vålådalen nature reserve. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Blåhammarkläppen
note: Summit right next to Blåhammarens fjällstation, about 740 m to its west. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Norra Helagsstöten
note: Helagsfjället's northern neighbour, about 3 km west-north-west of the main summit. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Ottfjället
note: Broad fjäll above Ottsjö, south of Åre; gentle and close to the road. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Städjan
note: Idre's landmark cone above the tree line; a gentle tour. No avalanche forecast covers this area: the trip planner still ranks it, marked caution and 'own judgement'. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Sonfjället
access: Sonfjället national park, east of Vemdalen
note: Isolated fjäll in its own national park; highest point Högfjället. No avalanche forecast covers this area: the trip planner still ranks it, marked caution and 'own judgement'. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked. Position: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap), approximate; height: Wikipedia.

name: Elgåhogna
access: From Grövelsjön; the summit is just across the border in Norway (Femundsmarka)
note: High, isolated summit in Femundsmarka on the Dalarna border. No avalanche forecast covers this area: the trip planner still ranks it, marked caution and 'own judgement'. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Høgeloft
note: The highest summit of Filefjell, on the Hemsedal–Lærdal–Vang border. Uses the Hallingdal bulletin. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Nibbi
note: Skogshorn's neighbour, 2.5 km to its west. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

links.title: Tips for ski touring in Hemsedal

name: Leinenøse
note: North of the Hemsedal valley. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Harahorn
note: One of the easier summits in Hemsedal. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

links.title: Tips for ski touring in Hemsedal

name: Slettind
note: One of the easier summits in Hemsedal. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position: OpenStreetMap (Mapcarta); height: Hemsedal tourist board.

links.title: Tips for ski touring in Hemsedal

name: Råskardfjellet
note: Broad fjäll west of the main Hemsedal valley. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

links.title: Tips for ski touring in Hemsedal

name: Svarthetta
note: North-west of Hemsedal, near Fosseberget. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Totten
note: The top of the Hemsedal ski area; touring from the lifts. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Storehorn
access: Hemsedal, south side of the valley
note: The pointed summit above Hemsedal village, next to Veslehorn. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Prestholtskarvet (Hallingskarvet)
note: The eastern end of the Hallingskarvet plateau, in the national park. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Folarskardnuten
note: The highest point of Hallingskarvet and of the old Buskerud county. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Einsetnuten
note: A short tour close to Geilo. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor (OpenStreetMap).

name: Blåbergi
access: Storestølen fjellhotell on Fv50 (parking 60.7095, 7.8521, about 1060 m)
note: North of Storestølen, across the Fv50 corridor north-west of Geilo. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit checked against Kartverket's terrain model (1802 m) and PeakVisor.

name: Såteggi
access: Fv50 north-west of Geilo, roadside parking
note: Low summit in Hallingskarvet national park, west along Fv50. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor, checked against Kartverket's terrain model (1415 m).

name: Urevassnutane (Urvassnuten)
note: Twin summits on the old Buskerud–Sogn og Fjordane border. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Summit position and height: PeakVisor, checked against Kartverket's terrain model (1769 m).

name: Gaustatoppen east couloirs
access: Gaustabanen (the railway inside the mountain) to the top, or skin up from Stavsro
note: The steep runs off the east side of Gaustatoppen, 40–52° per Visit Norway: expert terrain, rock bands and consequences. The normal route is listed separately as Gaustatoppen. Same summit point, checked against Kartverket's terrain model.

name: Røldalsåta
note: Popular high-mountain tour on even, open terrain with a long descent, often good spring snow; about 7 km. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position and height: Kartverket place names (Såta), checked against the terrain model (1401 m) and PeakVisor.

name: Stordalsnibba (Røldal)
note: Short tour straight from the ski centre, about 2.5 km; the south- and west-facing slopes get good spring snow. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1111 m).

name: Fjetlandsnuten
note: Quieter summit east of Røldal with steady climbing and open terrain for wide turns, about 4 km. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names and Peakbook, height checked against the terrain model (1282 m).

name: Midnuten (Røldal)
note: Local favourite following a ridge the whole way, so a fallback when bigger terrain is loaded; about 3 km. Not the 1463 m Midnuten by Breifonn. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1044 m).

name: Havrenos
access: Einerhaug cabin area, just west of Røldal centre
note: Short, gentle top above Røldalsvatnet for unsettled weather, families or a half day. Low, so it needs a good snow year. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (883 m).

name: Kistenuten
note: The classic Haukeli line: a long approach over plateau, water and scree to the couloir you can see from Haukeliseter, then a spectacular descent. Committing and avalanche-prone, so pick the day. About 7.5 km each way. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1648 m).

name: Store Nup
note: Easy plateau to start, then a steep final ridge that can need crampons on hard snow; broad, wide descent. About 3.5 km. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1656 m).

name: Vesle Nup
access: Small winter parking on Fv362 at Ulevå
note: One of the quickest ways onto the Nup massif: open plateau, no steep sections, a broad south ridge to the top and long open flanks down. About 5 km. ToppturNorge gives 1540 m, but Kartverket and PeakVisor both put the summit at about 1510 m. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names and PeakVisor, height checked against the terrain model (1506 m).

name: Verjesteinsnuten
note: Treeless from the car, then a steady broad ridge with moderate angles and no exposure; big views over Hardangervidda. About 5 km. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1650 m).

name: Sveigen
access: Pepparsteinen parking on the old road by Haukelitunnelen
note: Short and steep: 500 m in about 2 km, up a gully or round the flank; the north-west gully is the pick for the descent. Rated 3 here for the gully. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1538 m).

name: Stavsnuten
access: Parking west of Haukelitunnelen on E134
note: Efficient spring tour: up a stream valley, then a broad, open mountainside to the top and the same way down. About 3 km. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1658 m).

name: Nupsegga
access: Parking along E134 at Haukeli, where cleared
note: Longer day, about 7 km each way, over even, open terrain; the long open flats down are at their best on warm spring days. Aspect is set to 'varied' until checked, so the planner tests it against every avalanche problem. Position: Kartverket place names, height checked against the terrain model (1672 m).
